Class SlotGroupCategories

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.group.SlotGroupCategories
public final class SlotGroupCategories extends Object
The registry of SlotGroupResolvers, one primary per menu class. Shaped like MenuKit's MenuChrome: exact-class lookup, one primary resolver per class, SlotKit's resolvers for vanilla classes, and mods registering their own classes through register(Class, SlotGroupResolver).

A mod that adds slots to a vanilla menu and wants its slot group targeted by slot-group panels declares the group's category through extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver), which only adds categories and leaves the primary resolver's alone.

Exact class only

of(AbstractContainerMenu) looks up by menu.getClass(), with no walk up the class hierarchy. Vanilla's subclassing doesn't predict slot layout (CraftingMenu extends AbstractCraftingMenu, which extends RecipeBookMenu, but each concrete menu orders its slots its own way). Mods register for their own concrete menu classes.

Created slots publish here too

Every created slot group declares a SlotGroupCategory on its spec, and those groups are reported on whatever menu they sit. So of(AbstractContainerMenu) and categoriesBySlot(AbstractContainerMenu) name created and vanilla slots alike, using only SlotKit types. This is how one mod finds another's slots without knowing what kind they are.

Primary vs. extensions

Each class has at most one primary resolver (from register(Class, SlotGroupResolver)) and zero or more extension resolvers (from extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver)). of(AbstractContainerMenu) runs the primary first, then each extension, merging their output. Extensions can only add categories: one the primary already emitted is dropped from the extension, and one that two extensions both emit is dropped from both, each with a warning. So a category means the same slots in every mod.

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu> void register(Class<T> menuClass, SlotGroupResolver resolver)
      Registers the primary resolver for a concrete menu class. A second registration for the same class throws: which mod won would depend on load order. A second mod adds groups with extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver) instead.

      Called at mod init. SlotKit registers its vanilla resolvers from its own initializer; mods register from their ModInitializer.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the menu type
      Parameters:
      menuClass - the concrete menu class (typically the same class that's registered as a MenuType)
      resolver - the resolver

    • extend

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu> void extend(Class<T> menuClass, SlotGroupResolver resolver)
      Registers an extra resolver for a menu class, adding categories without replacing the primary. A class can have several extensions.

      For a mod that adds a slot to a vanilla menu (a FurnaceMenu, say) and wants its slot group targeted by slot-group panels under a category of its own. SlotKit's primary resolver for the vanilla menu is already registered and cannot be replaced, so extend adds to it.

      An extension adds categories and never redefines one. A category the primary already emits is dropped from the extension at resolve time, and a category two extensions both emit is dropped from both, each with a warning. So FURNACE_INPUT means the same slots in every mod.

      A class needs no primary for an extension to work.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the menu type
      Parameters:
      menuClass - the concrete menu class
      resolver - the extension resolver

    • declare

      public static void declare(SlotGroupCategory category)
      Publishes category to the registry so another mod can find it through all() without a menu open. Idempotent.

      SlotKit declares the vanilla constants at init, and a created group's category when the group registers, so a consumer that mints a category only calls this when it wants the category listed before anything is registered against it.

    • all

      public static List<SlotGroupCategory> all()
      Every category the registry knows: the vanilla constants, every category a created slot group declared, and anything a mod declare(SlotGroupCategory)d. Sorted by namespace then path so the listing is stable.

      This is the discovery half of the registry ("what kinds of slot exist?"), and it needs no open menu. The other half is per-menu: of(AbstractContainerMenu) for the slots in each category right now, categoriesBySlot(AbstractContainerMenu) for the inverse.

    • categoriesBySlot

      public static Map<net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot, SlotGroupCategory> categoriesBySlot(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      The category of each slot on menu, by slot identity: the inverse of of(AbstractContainerMenu), for a consumer walking menu.slots and asking "what is this one?" A slot in no category is absent. A vanilla slot and a created slot answer the same way, so a consumer can decide per category ("search PLAYER_INVENTORY and this mod's pockets; leave its elytra slot alone") without knowing which library put a slot there.

    • groups

      public static List<ResolvedSlotGroup> groups(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      Every slot group on menu, each with its own identity and its own slots. This is the anchor view, the one with geometry in it. A panel anchors to one of these; a group has a bounding box and a category does not.

      Resolution order: the player's own inventory slots, by their inventory index (hotbar, main grid, armor, offhand, on every menu that shows them, modded ones included), then the primary resolver for menu.getClass() (if any), then each extension in registration order, then the created groups on the menu. Each vanilla category yields one group; an extension's category that collides is dropped with a warning, as extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver) describes. Each created contribution yields its own group.

      Empty for menus where nothing resolves.

    • of

      public static Map<SlotGroupCategory, List<net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot>> of(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      Every category on menu with its slots. This is the search view, which unions a category's groups because "find me every inventory slot" wants the union. Vanilla slots first, created ones appended, never listed twice.

      For geometry use groups(AbstractContainerMenu) instead: a category's union spans scattered rectangles, so its bounding box means nothing.
